positions.title: Software Engineer Intern
positions.locationName: New York, New York, United States
positions.description:
- Streamlined insight creation workflow to be compatible with “hosted mills” as part of the Insights team.
- Solved a scalability issue of the Insights platform by constructing a proof of concept system that allows external
engineering teams to retain ownership of their code from creation through deployment.
- Integrated new workflow into existing insights services, promoting the use of Bloomberg Platform as a Service (BPaaS) to delegate responsibility within the insight creation process.

positions.title: Software Engineering Intern
positions.locationName: New York, New York, United States
positions.description:
As a Software Engineering Intern within the News Core Applications team, I:

- Leveraged distributed trace concepts to monitor system health of crucial workflows while working with the internal Distributed Trace team.
- Incorporated tracing infrastructure into widely hit company news services and augmented utilities to facilitate the process for future services. 
- Designed and implemented a C++ aggregator service to extract and analyze data, as well as published metrics to identify bottlenecks within workflows.

positions.title: Computer Vision Intern
positions.description:
During IAP, a month-long break between MIT semesters, I worked as a Computer Vision extern and participated in the agile development process at ISM Connect, where I:

- Optimized rescaling and cropping algorithms for face detectors and embedders for more accurate face detection.
- Implemented scripts to scrape image data and provide crops to use as facial recognition training data.
- Upgraded image classifier serializer to utilize JSON files while maintaining backwards compatibility.

positions.title: Research Intern
positions.description:
As a Summer Research Intern within the Advanced Capabilities and Systems Group (107) at MIT Lincoln Laboratory, I:

- Engineered solutions to autonomy problems through software improvements on 1/10-scale racecars 
- Developed a curriculum accessible to high school students for an introductory course on autonomous robotics using Python and ROS
- Co-instructed the MIT Beaver Works Summer Institute RACECAR course alongside Lincoln Laboratory staff.

positions.title: Explainer
positions.description:
As an Explainer at NYSCI, a science museum in Queens, I:

- Facilitated activities and interactions between visitors and the 400+ exhibits offered by NYSCI and clarified science concepts to people of all ages.
- Presented scientific demonstrations to the visitors, teaching about certain topics such as flight.
- Participated in activities such as career development workshops and STEM Nights, where I had the opportunity to network with professionals in a variety of career fields.

projects.title: LOV | VOL
projects.description: LOV | VOL is a web application that aims to increase the current New York City volunteer rate. As high school students, we have all faced the problem of wanting to dedicate time to causes we care about, but have come across difficulty in finding local opportunities efficiently. It is not only high school students who would benefit from an easier way to find volunteer opportunities. According to the Corporation for National & Community Service, the volunteer rate across the nation has been decreasing since 2011 and only 19.7% of New York residents volunteered consistently, the lowest rate of all 50 states. LOV | VOL enables New Yorkers to find and serve at volunteer locations around them through the use of the Google Maps API or based on their available free time through JQuery Calendar plugins. This web application incorporates elements of HTML/CSS, Javascript, and JQuery, as well as the use of different APIs in order to implement different features.
